question: A rectangle has a length that is four times its width. If the perimeter is 100 cm, what is the area of the rectangle?
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Given the ratio of Length to Width = 4 : 1

Perimeter in ratio units = 2 × (4 + 1) = 10 units

Actual perimeter is 100 cm, so 10 units = 100 cm ⇒ 1 unit = 10 cm

Therefore, Length = 40 cm and Width = 10 cm

Area = 40 × 10 = 400 cm²

**∴ The correct answer is 400 cm².**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Perimeter of the rectangle = 100 cm

Length (L) = 4 × Width (W)

**Formula Used:**

Perimeter = 2 × (L + W)

Area = L × W

 
 Length = 4W
 Width = W
 Perimeter = 100 cm
 Area = 400 cm²

**Calculations:**

⇒ 2 × (4W + W) = 100

⇒ 2 × 5W = 100

⇒ 10W = 100

⇒ W = 10 cm

⇒ L = 4 × 10 = 40 cm

⇒ Area = 40 × 10 = 400 cm²

**∴ The correct answer is 400 cm².**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Properties of a Rectangle

In a rectangle, opposite sides are parallel and equal in length. Furthermore, all four interior angles are exactly 90°.

Diagonal of a Rectangle

The length of a diagonal divides the rectangle into two right-angled triangles. It can be found using Pythagoras theorem: d = √(L² + W²).

Perimeter and Area Relation

For a given fixed perimeter, a square (where length equals width) will always enclose the maximum possible area among all rectangular shapes.
